        "title": "Continual-ARC task-42d0526a: stamp colored mask on zero matches",
        "content": "Task-42d0526a rule (confirmed by three demos and correct test): Treat the existing non-background colored object as a stencil: its colored cells define the mask; ignore all uncolored cells in its bounding box. At every in-bounds translation where every mask cell overlays background color 0, recolor those mask positions to the object color. Preserve the source object and all other cells. Overlapping matches simply produce the same recoloring. Demo backgrounds used 0 with other noise colors (5 or 9); the match criterion was all mask positions are 0. Test source was three vertical 1s; marking every vertical run of three zeros solved. Additional confirmed recurrence: a 16x25 grid had background 9, scattered zeros as targets/noise, and a six-cell color-1 source mask in bbox 3x3: 111 / ..1 / .11 (dots are ignored). Scanning every in-bounds translation where all six mask positions were exactly 0 found three matches at zero-based top-left (6,8), (10,16), and (13,15); recoloring those positions to 1 was confirmed correct. Thus target color is literal 0, not necessarily the dominant background; retain all other cells and the source. Additional confirmed recurrence: in a 25x13 test, color 5 formed an 8-cell stencil in a 5x4 bbox: ..5. / .5.. / .55. / 55.. / ..55 (dots ignored). Applying it only where all stencil cells were zero produced matches at zero-based top-left (2,1) and (12,1); this output was confirmed correct. The grid contained background 9 and unrelated zeros; target remains literal zero.\nAdditional confirmed recurrence: a 29x11 input used background 6 and a source color-8 2x2 stencil [88/80], so only the three top-left/upper-right/lower-left cells form the mask and the bottom-right bbox cell is ignored. Recolor to 8 at all in-bounds positions where these mask cells are all 0. Zero-based bbox top-left matches: (1,4), (3,0), (5,1), (6,1), (6,5), (7,0), (7,1), (8,0), (10,7), (13,6), (13,7), (14,3), (14,4), (14,5), (14,6), (15,3), (16,6), (16,7), (17,6), (17,7), (18,4), (20,2), (22,2), (22,8), (26,5). Correct output confirmed. This reiterates that grid background can be another color and the target remains literal zero; preserve non-mask bbox cells and all other cells.\n\nRecurrence confirmation (2026-10-20): solved a 13x13 test with background 8, literal-zero target cells, and color-5 stencil `555 / .5. / .5.` (mask offsets (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1); dots ignored). The four valid all-zero placements had bbox top-lefts (2,1), (2,2), (2,4), and (4,3), zero-based. Recolor only those stencil positions to 5; preserve source at rows 7-9, cols 9-11 and all other cells. First submission accepted.\n\nRecurrence confirmation (2026-10-20): task-42d0526a test was 28x13 with background 9, literal-zero target sites, and source color-8 stencil bbox 6x2: `8. / 88 / 8. / 88 / 88 / 8.` (dots are ignored; 9 mask cells). All-zero placements were found at zero-based bbox top-lefts (9,11) and (14,0). Recolor only the stencil cells at these placements to 8, preserving all other cells and the source; submission accepted.\n\nRecurrence confirmation (2026-10-20): solved 27x20 test, background 9 and literal zero target cells; source color 6 mask in 2x4 bbox with offsets (0,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1,3), i.e. `66../..66` (dots ignored). Scan every in-bounds translation requiring all four mask positions to be exactly 0, then recolor those positions to 6. Matches at zero-based bbox top-lefts (2,14),(3,15),(5,1),(6,10),(7,7),(11,15),(14,13),(15,4),(15,5),(15,6),(16,1),(18,13),(21,3),(21,11),(25,5).       "continual_arc_task_12c29693_recurring_object_recoloring_puzzle_unsolved": {

        "content": "Task-12c29693 recurring object recoloring. Recurrent behavior: preserve grid except recolor a single non-background object to the color of a distinctive elongated L/bar component. This task was previously unsolved after 8 demo pairs; that test's failed guesses are retained below. A plausible rule is that when identical-shape objects occur in different colors, recolor the copy farther from the long L/bar marker into the marker color. Treat this as a useful hypothesis, not a universal rule: other demos had less-obvious target selection.\n\nDemonstrations from this fresh instance (input object -> output color; background omitted):\n1) bg3, a 7-cell color1 object at bottom-left (rows16-18, c5-7; shape rows XX/.XX/XXX) became color2. Long marker color2 was an L/bar near upper-right.\n2) bg6, top-left irregular 14-cell color2 object became color7; marker color7 was long bent bar at lower-left.\n3) bg0, 2-cell color6 domino at r4 c14-15 became color9; marker color9 was a long bent bar at top-left. There were other color6 cells/pairs, so simplistic largest-of-color does not explain every target.\n4) bg3, 7-cell color0 object at rows16-18 c7-9 (shape 2/3/2) became color9; marker color9 was long bent object near top-center.\n5) bg6, 3-cell color5 L at bottom-left (r17 c0-1, r18 c0) became color2; marker color2 was long L at top-left.\n6) bg7, 3-cell color9 L at rows20-21 c6-7 became color1; marker color1 was large L/bar at bottom-left.\n7) bg4, 2x4 color7 rectangle at rows10-13 c16-17 became color3; marker color3 was long vertical bar with horizontal top segment at bottom-right.\n8) bg9, singleton color4 at r0c12 became color1; marker color1 was L/bar top-left. Another singleton color0 at r0c3 stayed unchanged; target was farther from marker.\nThese reinforce recoloring to a long L/bar object's color; distance and duplicate-shape relations may be important, but full selector rule remains uncertain.\n\nEarlier test recorded on previous recurrence (11x17,bg7): main color2 L at r6 c12-16 plus r7-10 c12; color0 7-cell mask rows1-3 c7-9 = ..#/###/###; color3 L triomino r1 c13-14,r2 c14 and a separate color3 vertical pair r9-10 c6; color8 rectangle 4x2 at r5-8 c2-3, vertical trio r6-8 c10, and 7-cell shape at r8c16 and r9-10 c14-16 identical to color0 mask; color4 singleton r10c0. Do not repeat. Those failures show matching-shape mapping is not enough unless correct copy/marker and target selection are identified.\n\nParsing care: all submitted grids must have consistent dimensions; initial answer here was rejected as invalid because last row had 28 rather than 29 cells. Check row lengths before submission.\n\nAdditional recurrence evidence (new 8-demo stream; selector still not fully solved):\n- Demo 1: bg0; marker color9 is L/bar at lower-right. Recolored one large color2 object in upper-right (rows6-10 approx cols17-21) to 9; another small color2 pair near marker stayed unchanged.\n- Demo 2: bg6; marker color9 L at lower-right. Recolored a color5 irregular object near center-right (approx rows13-15, cols12-17) to 9. Other color5 pieces stayed.\n- Demo 3: bg2; marker color6 L at left around row3. Recolored irregular color3 5-cell object at rows1-2, cols7-9 to 6.\n- Demo 4: bg2; marker color1 L at upper-left (vertical c6, horizontal r5). Recolored color8 horizontal 3-cell object at row5 cols11-13 to 1. There was another identical 3-cell horizontal color8 object at row3 cols1-3; the farther copy was recolored. This supports an identical-shape/farther-copy selector in at least some instances.\n- Demo 5: bg8; marker color5 L at upper-right. Recolored irregular 5-cell color0 object at rows1-4, cols3-4 to 5.\n- Demo 6: bg2; marker color4 L upper-left. Recolored large 11-cell color6 object (rows8-9, cols13-18) to 4.\n- Demo 7: bg0; marker color8 L upper-left. Recolored color5 vertical domino at rows6-7, col24 to 8.\n- Demo 8: bg4; marker color3 L upper-right (vertical c15, horizontal r4). Recolored a 3-cell L-shaped color0 object at r8c10/r9c9-10 to 3. This further supports farther-copy for some selector cases.\n\nFailed fresh test after 8 demos, not solved (8/8 attempts used): bg8, marker color1 is large L/bar at rows19-24, c21 plus row19 c21-28. Single-object-to-marker-color guesses all failed. Failed candidates were: (1) color0 14-cell irregular object rows14-17 cols20-23; (2) color5 4-cell L object cells (18,12),(19,11-12),(20,12); (3) color3 vertical 5-bar at rows0-4,c11; (4) color3 L triomino at (8,18),(9,18-19); (5) color5 L triomino at (7,21),(7,22),(8,21); (6) color3 horizontal domino at row0 cols1-2; (7) color0 vertical 3-bar rows5-7,c12; (8) color0 vertical domino rows4-5,c0. These failures specifically show that simple alignment-to-marker, nearest/farthest object, and guessed far-copy pairs are insufficient; don't repeat these candidate changes without new reasoning.\n\nSelector remains unresolved: recoloring one object to distinctive L/bar marker's color is strongly consistent; identical-shape farther copy is supported by several examples and a prior accepted case, but cannot be applied indiscriminately (the current test had several plausible matching shapes, and all eight guesses failed). This reinforces the farther-duplicate selector confirmed in other solved recurrences above.\n\n\nNew recurrence confirmed (19x14, background 2): special marker color4 forms an L, horizontal row13 c10-13 and vertical c10 rows13-18. Two identical 6-cell objects share mask ##/##/#./#.: color8 at rows13-16,c8-9 (cells c8-9 in rows13-14, then c8 in rows15-16), and color7 at rows15-18,c12-13 (c12-13 in rows15-16, then c12 in rows17-18). For this selection, compare copy centers/distances to the marker, not simply closest boundary cell: the chosen 8 copy’s center is farther from marker’s center than the 7 copy’s. This is further confirmation of the farther identical-shape-copy selector (shape match + farther copy -> marker color).\n\nFive demos from this recurrence (use as supporting evidence; target is one non-background component and output uses the prominent L/bar color): D1 background2, marker6 (large L at rows9-13 near left); upper-left color5 pattern recolored to6. D2 bg1, marker9 L at top-left; a lone color8 cell (r16,c11) changed to9. D3 bg1, marker2 L at bottom-left; color0 horizontal domino at r27,c16-17 changed to2. D4 bg2, marker8 long bent bar at bottom-left; color7 horizontal triple at r3,c19-21 changed to8. D5 bg6, marker3 L at upper-left; a color7 3-cell L at rows7-8,c24-25 changed to3. These demos alone do not reveal target selection; preserve the duplicate-shape/farther-copy hypothesis as well-supported but avoid arbitrary candidates.\n\n\nConfirmed recurrence solved at zero wrong submissions (14x23, bg=8). Marker was the color5 L/bar component: horizontal run at row10 cols18-22, with vertical extension at col18 rows10-13 (8 cells total). Two identical 2x3 solid rectangles were present: color1 at rows12-13 cols5-7 and color7 at rows12-13 cols20-22. Recolor ONLY the farther copy (color1, lower-left) to marker color5; leave the nearer color7 rectangle and all other cells unchanged. Accepted output confirms same-shape farther-from-marker selector, using object/component centers (the color1 rectangle is far from the color5 marker; the color7 rectangle is close). Other components include color6 irregular 13-cell cluster, color9 vertical-ish object and separate stripe, several color3 objects; none changed. This was solved immediately, no demos required.\n",

        "content": "Task-45f42459, solved. A ray that meets a target cell stops there and recolors that cell to 4; the target cells' offset pattern is copied to the opposing bar's rows/columns, where rays run to the far edge without a 4 endpoint. Demo 1: 3 pairs at top row cols1-2 and bottom row cols5-6; single 2 at (8,2); output drew 2 vertical rays at cols2 and 6, recolored marker at (8,2) to 4. Demo 2: 8 bars at right edge rows0-4 and left edge rows10-14; 1 markers at (10,5),(12,3),(13,6),(14,4). Output draws horizontal 1 rays inward for marker-bearing offsets from left bar and copies that offset pattern to the opposing right bar; marker endpoints become 4. Solved test: 10x6 background6; 5 left bar rows0-3, 5 right bar rows6-9; 2 targets at (6,1),(7,2),(8,1),(9,1). Output fills rows0-3 cols1-5 with 2; at rows6-9 draws leftward from col4 toward each target, 2 in between and changes each target to 4; other cells unchanged. Generalize cautiously: identify edge bars/axes, align offsets across opposite bars, use isolated target color to draw rays; preserve border bars/background and recolor endpoint target cells to 4.\n\nCaution from a failed recurrence (2026-10-20): an input with top bar c3-5, bottom bar c0-2, and targets at (r3,c4),(r7,c3),(r7,c5) on a 14x11 grid did NOT match any of these simple projections.
